title: Scientific verification: selective safe rollback — path-limited restore, path-limited stash, content-capture for mixed files, and the banned blanket restore (negative control)

problem.description: EXP-000012 (latest version v2, the technical revision) claims: (1) rollback must be SELECTIVE and SAFE — restore exactly what the agent changed (git restore -- <path>, git stash push -- <paths>, or re-apply captured pre-edit content), never repo-wide git checkout . / git reset --hard which destroy the user's unrelated uncommitted work; (2) when the agent's edit and the user's pre-existing WIP share ONE file, prefer restoring just the agent's hunks — the content-capture path (capture before the first edit, re-apply on failure) is the non-interactive mechanism; (3) the rollback must be CONFIRMED by re-running the exact failing check — the ORIGINAL error must reproduce as the known-green marker; (4) git restore -p and path-limited stash semantics are doc-verifiable. The v2 revision REMOVED the arbitrary two-attempt rewrite threshold (continuation is governed by information gain — process guidance, plan item V3, not mechanically testable per the record itself).
problem.symptoms: agent rewrites spiral; user's uncommitted work destroyed by blanket restores; failed fixes stacked on unknown state; loss of attribution
problem.expectedBehavior: V1a: after a failed agent edit, `git restore -- lib.js` (plus removing the agent's scratch file) leaves the USER's uncommitted WIP in app.js intact, removes exactly the agent's edit, and the ORIGINAL failing check reproduces. V1b: `git stash push -- lib.js` achieves the same with the change recoverable in the stash. V1c (negative control): the banned `git checkout -- .` destroys the user's WIP along with the agent's edit. V1d: when user WIP and the agent edit share one file, capturing the pre-edit content BEFORE the edit and re-applying it on failure restores the user's hunk and removes the agent's hunk, leaving the working tree at exactly the user's WIP. V2: the locally installed git documentation (man git-restore / man git-stash for git 2.53.0) documents path-scoped working-tree restore, interactive hunk selection, and stash push with pathspec.
problem.actualBehavior: to be measured by real execution on the user's machine through the bridge
problem.facts: git restore restores specified paths in the working tree from a restore source (default: the index); git stash push accepts pathspecs; the user's machine has git 2.53.0 with local man pages (phrases pre-verified via bridge probes); all experiments run in mktemp scratch dirs — nothing in the user's workspace is touched.
problem.assumptions: git 2.53.0 semantics match the VM dry-run environment (git 2.47.3) for the operations used (restore, stash push with pathspec, checkout -- .); man pages are present on the user's machine (verified by probe).
problem.environment: user's machine via the bridge extension: Linux, git 2.53.0, local man pages; VM dry-runs on git 2.47.3
problem.constraints: every experiment writes only to mktemp -d scratch dirs (removed on exit); no workspace files touched; V2 uses local documentation (no network); outputs below the 20KB truncation limit.

hypothesis.text: All five cases pass on real execution: the two selective mechanisms (path-limited restore, path-limited stash) preserve the user's uncommitted work while removing exactly the agent's edit and reproducing the original error; the banned blanket restore demonstrably destroys user work; the content-capture path handles the mixed-file case leaving the working tree at exactly the user's WIP; and the installed git's own documentation states the path-scoped restore and stash-pathspec semantics.
hypothesis.expectedObservation: markers: V1a-SELECTIVE-RESTORE-VERIFIED, V1b-PATH-LIMITED-STASH-VERIFIED, V1c-BLANKET-RESTORE-DAMAGE-CONFIRMED, V1d-CONTENT-CAPTURE-ROLLBACK-VERIFIED, V2-DOC-VERIFIED
hypothesis.supportingEvidence: VM dry-runs (git 2.47.3) reproduce all four experimental markers; all V2 man-page phrases were pre-verified present on the user's machine via bridge probes (git-restore: 'Restore working tree files', 'Restore specified paths in the working tree with some contents from a restore source', 'Interactively select hunks'; git-stash: 'new stash entry', 'pathspec', 'stash push ... pathspec').
hypothesis.contradictingEvidence: none observed in dry-runs; V2 cannot be dry-run in the VM (no git man pages there) — its phrases were verified directly on the target machine instead.

strategy: Five cases, all staged in the run sandbox: V1a/V1b selective rollback mechanisms, V1c the banned-command negative control, V1d the mixed-file content-capture path, V2 local documentation inspection (man pages of the installed git). V3 (continuation criteria) is process guidance per the record's own plan and is not mechanically testable — no case, noted in the analysis.
